recentItems.title: Houthi Missiles Strike Saudi Weapons Trucks At Yemen Border: Huge Explosions Seen In Rebels' Video
recentItems.description:
In a series of assaults on Saudi Arabia, Yemen's Houthi rebel group, which receives backing from Iran, injured over 70 individuals and sparked blazes at oil infrastructure and utility sites within the kingdom.

The assault marked a significant intensification in the ongoing conflict between a key ally of the United States and the Iranian-backed militia.

Moreover, it posed a risk of worsening instability in a region that has already endured nearly three years of warfare, potentially inflicting additional damage on the global economy.

The Houthis reported that they launched ballistic missiles at trucks associated with Saudi Arabia, which were transporting military supplies, at a border crossing close to Al-Wadiah, situated on the Saudi-Yemen frontier.

Video footage documented the instant a fragmentation missile hit the trucks filled with military gear, triggering a series of explosive blasts and releasing thick clouds of smoke into the atmosphere.

Weeks of conflict have intensified the strain on already scarce global oil supplies, as the Houthis focus their attacks on a key shipping lane utilized by Saudi Arabia for oil exports to international markets. 

This situation is further complicated by restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz, which are a consequence of the ongoing US-Iran war.

The attacks hit Saudi oil facilities connected to an alternative route, the Bab el-Mandeb, a strategic waterway off the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula that connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
